ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The diagram below shows three identical 1.0 L containers filled with the indicated amounts of gas. The stopcocks connecting the containers are originally closed and the gases are all at 25°C. Assume ideal behavior. The stopcocks are opened. If the tubing connecting the containers has negligible volume, by what percentage will the pressure exerted by the neon gas decrease?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are three identical circular containers connected horizontally, with a closed stopcock between every two containers. The left container is labeled “20.0 g He”, the middle container is labeled “40.0 g Ne”, and the right container is labeled “30.0 g NO”. The problem text states that the volume of each container is 1.0 L, the gases are all at 25°C, the volume of the connecting tubes is negligible, and after the stopcocks are opened, the gases can diffuse into all three containers. Reasoning: What is asked for is the pressure exerted by the neon gas itself, that is, the change in the partial pressure of the neon gas. The amount of substance of neon gas does not change, the temperature does not change, and an ideal gas satisfies P = nRT/V, so the pressure of the neon gas is inversely proportional to the volume it can occupy. Initially the neon gas is only in the middle 1.0 L container; after the stopcocks are opened, the neon gas can occupy three 1.0 L containers, with a total volume of 3.0 L. Therefore P_final,Ne / P_initial,Ne = 1.0/3.0 = 1/3. The proportion by which the pressure decreases is 1 - 1/3 = 2/3 = 66.7%, approximately 67%.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: three connected equal-volume bulbs are shown, labeled 20.0 g He, 40.0 g Ne, and 30.0 g NO, with stopcocks between them. Use the text fact that each bulb is 1.0 L, the gases are at the same 25°C, the stopcocks are initially closed, and tubing volume is negligible. Neon initially occupies 1.0 L; after opening, the same neon moles occupy 3.0 L. Since T and n for Ne are unchanged, P_final,Ne/P_initial,Ne = 1.0/3.0 = 1/3. Therefore the fractional decrease is 1 - 1/3 = 2/3, or about 67%.
